resources.string: Allows Aura to observe the screen, understand the UI structure, and perform safe actions on your behalf using accessibility actions like click, scroll, and input text.

Lets Aura read on-screen text so it can comment on what you are doing. Aura sends this text to the server address you configured, and only while screen observation is switched on inside the Aura app. Password fields are never read.
Occasional remarks from Aura when something on screen seems worth mentioning.
Your conversation, memory and personality live on your Aura server — the same one, wherever you open this.
Aura needs the address of your server before it can talk. You can change it later without reinstalling.
This address uses plain HTTP to a remote host. Your messages and token would travel unencrypted. Use https:// for anything outside your home network.
Let Aura reach you when the app is closed. Checked periodically, not continuously.
Let Aura read what is on screen so it can comment when something is worth mentioning. Off by default. Also requires enabling Aura in system Accessibility settings.
Set by AURA_SERVER_AUTH_TOKEN on the server. Stored encrypted on this device and never sent anywhere but your server.
Send images as well as text. Uses far more data; text alone is usually enough.
For example https://aura.onrender.com, or http://192.168.1.10:8000 on your home network.
